svg.text: Putting It All Together: Zero-Touch to a Fully Managed Edge System
One device identity • four FDO-aware phases • each phase asks only for the FSIMs it needs
Sets up and credentials the device for everything that follows
Same operator, same device record as the
Onboarding Service; it minted the agent
credential it now expects to see.
Device identity: FDO credential in the TPM (DAK, from factory DI), shared by every FDO client below; credential reuse keeps it valid
← fdo.bmo: UKI (kernel + installer initrd + FDO client)
FDO client (ROE): go-fdo-endpoint in the initrd
→ fdo.credentials: SSH host public keys + IP
← fdo.payload: full OS ISO → RAM disk
← = owner to device → = device to owner
stock installer (e.g. Fedora Anaconda, Ubuntu Subiquity, openSUSE Agama)
Installs the OS from the delivered ISO, as the delivered config says; keeps the FDO-registered SSH host keys
+ Installs the Management Agent and enables it to start at boot
from the OS image / its repo, or the agent package delivered in Stage 2; one more line in the kickstart / autoinstall
the application layer: the agent runs FDO one more time
Same TPM device credential → TO1 / TO2 (credential reuse)
Never asks for fdo.bmo or the OS payloads, so it never gets them;
earlier phases never asked for the agent credential, so they never got it.
Connects to the DMS at the delivered URL,
Takes orders: install, update, report, run
The part that already exists and is in use today
⑥ Final state: device in service (as in the FDO specification's entity diagram)
From bare metal, zero-touch: OS installed • SSH identity verified • agent credentialed and connected
No manual agent install, no hand-copied credentials, one device identity throughout
The twist: the application layer (Stage 4) is the last step in the FDO architecture, yet it was the first thing FDO was used for.
BMO (Stages 1–3) now delivers the OS and the agent, so the whole chain from bare metal to managed device is one zero-touch flow.
